short_name: USCG Cybersecurity in the Marine Transportation System
summary: Designate Cybersecurity Officer; annual Cybersecurity Assessment; Coast Guard-approved Cybersecurity Plan; account security/MFA, encryption, logging, patching, segmentation, supply chain, penetration testing, Cyber Incident Response Plan, drills/exercises, training; report reportable cyber incidents.
applies_to: Owners/operators of U.S.-flagged vessels, facilities and OCS facilities required to have security plans under 33 CFR parts 104, 105, 106 (not foreign-flagged vessels).
size_thresholds: No size threshold; applicability tied to MTSA security plan requirement.
status: Effective July 16, 2025. Training by Jan 12, 2026 and annually; Cybersecurity Assessment and Cybersecurity Plan submission no later than July 16, 2027 (per current eCFR).

short_name: TSA rail and public transportation cybersecurity Security Directives
citation: SD 1580-21-01E (freight rail), SD 1582-21-01E (public transportation/passenger rail), SD 1580/82-2022-01E (mitigation actions & testing); authority 49 U.S.C. 114
summary: Designate cybersecurity coordinator, report cyber incidents to CISA within 24 hours, cyber incident response plan, vulnerability assessment; 2022-01 series: TSA-approved Cybersecurity Implementation Plan (segmentation, access control, continuous monitoring, patching), assessment program and testing.
applies_to: TSA-designated higher-risk freight railroads, passenger rail and rail transit owner/operators.
size_thresholds: Applicability set by TSA risk designation, not by employee/revenue thresholds.

summary: 01 series: cybersecurity coordinator, 24-hour incident reporting to CISA, vulnerability assessment; 02 series: mitigation actions, cyber incident response/contingency planning and testing, architecture review.
applies_to: TSA-designated critical hazardous liquid and natural gas pipeline owner/operators (NAICS 486).

short_name: TSA aviation cybersecurity emergency amendments/security program changes
citation: TSA security programs (49 CFR parts 1542, 1544, 1546) - content is SSI
summary: Airport and aircraft operators must implement approved cyber implementation plans: IT/OT segmentation, access control, continuous monitoring/detection, risk-based patching; builds on prior CISA incident reporting, cyber POC, IR plan and vulnerability assessment requirements.
size_thresholds: By TSA regulatory status, not size.
status: Issued Mar 7, 2023; specific current versions are Sensitive Security Information and not publicly posted.

citation: CBP program (voluntary); Minimum Security Criteria incl. cybersecurity
summary: Voluntary supply-chain security certification with cybersecurity, business partner, and risk assessment criteria.
applies_to: Highway, rail and sea carriers, consolidators, OTIs/NVOCCs, marine port authority/terminal operators, customs brokers.

short_name: DOT unfair/deceptive practices authority (airlines, ticket agents)
summary: DOT (not FTC) enforces unfair/deceptive practices, including privacy and data security practices, against air carriers and ticket agents.
applies_to: Air carriers, foreign air carriers, ticket agents.

citation: 32 CFR Part 170; DFARS 252.204-7021 (48 CFR rule, 90 FR 43560)
summary: Requires CMMC status (Level 1 self; Level 2 self or C3PAO; Level 3 DIBCAC) as a condition of DoD award; Level 2 = NIST SP 800-171 R2, Level 3 adds NIST SP 800-172.
applies_to: DoD contractors and subcontractors that process, store or transmit FCI or CUI on contractor information systems (flows down the supply chain).
size_thresholds: No small-business exemption. Applies to DoD solicitations/contracts above the micro-purchase threshold; excludes procurements exclusively for COTS items (32 CFR 170.3(c)).
status: 32 CFR 170 effective Dec 16, 2024; DFARS acquisition rule effective Nov 10, 2025 = start of Phase 1. Phase 2 begins one year after Phase 1 (Nov 10, 2026), Phase 3 one year later, Phase 4 (full) one year after that. Phase 2 suspended: the DoD (Department of War) CIO memorandum of 2026-07-13 suspended the Phase 2 transition planned for 2026-11-10. Under DoD Class Deviation 2026-O0025, Revision 3 (DFARS 240.371-5), clause 252.204-7021 is used until 2028-11-09 only when a program office requires a specific CMMC level, and from 2028-11-10 whenever contractor systems process, store, or transmit FCI or CUI. During the suspension requiring activities may require Level 1 (Self) or Level 2 (Self); SP 800-171 Rev. 2 under DFARS 252.204-7012 still applies. 32 CFR Part 170 is unchanged.

citation: 17 CFR 229.106 (Reg S-K Item 106); Form 8-K Item 1.05 (Release 33-11216, 88 FR 51896)
summary: Annual 10-K disclosure of cyber risk management, strategy and governance; Form 8-K Item 1.05 disclosure of material cybersecurity incidents.
applies_to: Exchange Act reporting companies (public issuers), including public companies in any sector.
size_thresholds: No exemption by size; smaller reporting companies received a later Item 1.05 compliance date (June 15, 2024 vs. Dec 18, 2023).
status: In force; effective Sept 5, 2023. No rescission found in Federal Register as of 2026-09-25.
